title: Stabilize PNN-v1-alpha1 across initializations
research_question: Can a controlled stabilization change reduce PNN-v1 seed sensitivity on ECG200 without abandoning the Q.ANT-native hierarchical low-fan-in design?
hypothesis: The main near-term limitation is learned-model instability rather than Q.ANT/reference mismatch. A preregistered stabilization intervention should reduce across-seed variance while preserving compactness and Q.ANT-native execution.
design_constraints: Keep the hierarchical low-fan-in Q.ANT Fourier/KAN structure.
Compare alpha1 unchanged against exactly one stabilization intervention.
Use more fixed seeds than Exp001.
Do not tune candidates against TEST accuracy during the run.
Keep parameter count close to alpha1 unless the intervention explicitly requires otherwise.
primary_metric: Across-seed Q.ANT accuracy stability (standard deviation), interpreted together with mean Q.ANT accuracy.
success_criteria: The stabilized condition must reduce Q.ANT accuracy standard deviation versus alpha1 without a material loss in mean Q.ANT accuracy. Exact intervention and tolerance must be frozen in the Exp002 implementation before execution.
hardware_boundary: Software/simulation-backend experiment only; no real photonic hardware performance claim.
next_gate: Implement and review PNN-v1 Exp002 before adding it to the guarded approval allowlist.
